reviews.text: An extraordinary and chilling documentary, “The Act of Killing” chronicles exactly that in unprecedented ways.
reviews.author: Diane Carson

reviews.text: A rare example of an international true crime story that got the documentary film treatment, and an even rarer example of killers participating in a film and reenacting their crimes.
reviews.author: Olivia B. Waxman

reviews.text: "The Act of Killing” is unquestionably the most innovative piece of documentary filmmaking to come out this decade.
reviews.author: Wael Khairy

reviews.text: Joshua Oppenheimer’s elegantly disturbing investigation.
reviews.author: Vadim Rizov

reviews.text: A potent exposé that unveils one of the darker secrets of our world.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: The results are astonishing, terrifying and eventually profound, as the men start to confront their own pasts.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: The bloodbath and coup in Indonesia were the outcome of the drive by US imperialism to gain control of the natural and strategic resources of the archipelago, known as the "Jewel of Asia."
reviews.author: Joanne Laurier

reviews.text: The Act of Killing might be the most powerful and cathartic documentary I've ever seen.
reviews.author: Dustin Chang

reviews.text: Demonstrates with chilling authenticity that nobody thinks they're the bad guys.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: Everything that occurs in The Act of Killing is outrageous and offensive and inhumane.
reviews.author: Richard Propes

reviews.text: There are few films that have legitimately left a chill down my spine. The Act of Killing is one of them.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: There's a terrifying singularity to Joshua Oppenheimer's examination of trauma, memory and denial.
reviews.author: Alison Gillmor

reviews.text: The Act of Killing is a brutal, unrelenting cinematic experience. It can't be reduced to one simple trope or theme and really can't even evoke one overriding, overarching emotion.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: The Act of Killing is important and unique in illustrating the banality of evil.
reviews.author: Hanna B

reviews.text: Soaked in blood and haunted by ghosts, The Act of Killing is not an easy watch at all. But it is an incredibly rewarding one; this truly is cinema at its most important.
reviews.author: Christopher Preston

reviews.text: One of the great, unique, often intangible and sometimes scary potentials of the film medium is the way that cinematic artifice can achieve something more profound than mere fact.
reviews.author: Daniel Barnes

reviews.text: A disturbingly comfortable voyage into the mindset of evil and the psychology of a murderer(s), Oppenheimer's film is like nothing you'll have ever seen before.
reviews.author: Patrick Gamble

reviews.text: The Act of Killing is the only 100% original work of cinema to come out this year.
reviews.author: Scott Marks

reviews.text: Beyond this intellectual actualisation, I can't help but think that the film falls short of its supposed brilliance. Surely watching socially or politically charged documentaries should achieve something more than cognition!
reviews.author: Tara Judah

reviews.text: If Oppenheimer's aim is to question and investigate what life the past has in the present, he has succeeded in a staggeringly original way.
reviews.author: Dave Calhoun

reviews.text: To take Anwar's own dramatic projection of his gradual humanisation seems a much more murky and less conclusive process than Oppenheimer wants to tidily present us with.
reviews.author: PJ Nabarro

reviews.text: It all makes sense when you submit yourself to Oppenheimer's bizarre, tragic, and eye-opening experiment.
reviews.author: Thrillist Entertainment Staff

reviews.text: What makes the film so powerful, and so provocative, is that the people whose imaginations spawned these spectacular images killed hundreds of people.
reviews.author: Pat Padua

reviews.text: Philosophically rich, visually stunning, emotionally devastating.
reviews.author: Eve Tushnet

reviews.text: Rarely has the full potential of cinema itself been brought home so forcefully.
reviews.author: Steve Erickson

reviews.text: The result is something we've never seen before - a new type of film - call it psycho-documentary - that's not just about mass crimes but the state of mind that produced them.
reviews.author: Lynden Barber

reviews.text: [An] innovative piece of filmmaking so breathtakingly daring and powerful, it replaces your oxygen with awe.
reviews.author: Larushka Ivan-Zadeh

reviews.text: The visual highs and emotional payoffs contained within the film are well worth slogging through its slow patches.
reviews.author: Abby Olcese

reviews.text: Fascinated by the action on screen, we might almost overlook the skill with which The Act of Killing has been conceived, edited, and directed.
reviews.author: Francine Prose

reviews.text: The Act of Killing is as much a movie about the movies as it is a movie about real-life horror.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: It's graceful and eloquent, and it has as its subject a lierotten culture-not merely in the official cant, but in the hearts and minds of even the poorest people.
reviews.author: Michael Atkinson

reviews.text: Through its audacious and confrontational conceit, Killing offers piercing insights into the minds of murderers.
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: Once you grasp just what is being enacted on the screen, The Act of Killing becomes something like a candy-colored moral migraine. An existential nausea is inevitable.
reviews.author: J. Hoberman

reviews.text: A warped phantasmagoria of denial that is essential viewing, even though it's almost impossible to watch.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: Maddening, sorrowful, brilliant, and unforgettable.
reviews.author: Dan Schindel

reviews.text: The film of the year, if not the decade, if not documentary history.
reviews.author: Rima Sabina Aouf

reviews.text: Most challengingly, though, there is something palpably cathartic about the ritual of the re-creations.
reviews.author: Jonathan Kiefer

reviews.text: One of the most audacious documentaries ever made, this mind-boggling film forces us to examine our opinions about human history far beyond the events covered on-screen.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Bizarre documentary featuring Hollywood-inspired, interpretive song and dance reenactments of ethnic cleansing in Indonesia.
reviews.author: Kam Williams

reviews.text: Raw and wrenching but narrow retro-focus on the slaughter of millions of Indonesian leftists in collusion with the CIA. But much like Out Of The Furnace, locating truth evasively within the masses, rather than tracing US government and economic roots.
reviews.author: Prairie Miller

reviews.text: It's a long and uncomfortable journey, but The Act of Killing is also fascinating, using film as a hall of mirrors to reveal not just the faces, but the twisted souls, of murderers.
reviews.author: Damon Wise

reviews.text: Oppenheimer demonstrates how easily the passive spectator can become an unlikely abettor, and the great cause of his film is to make his actors and audience recognize their moral culpability.
reviews.author: Christopher Gray

reviews.text: [The film explores] what happens when you give those who have done something terrible (in this case, killing thousands) a forum through which to tell their story to see if a new perspective changes their attitude.
reviews.author: Allison Loring

reviews.text: The shock of the final scene must be left unspoken; suffice to say its impact exceeds even the nightmarish queasiness which this brilliant and horrible film has striven to contain.
reviews.author: Anthony Quinn

reviews.text: [There is] an emotional disconnect that seems downright dangerous in a film about genocide.
reviews.author: Jennifer Merin

reviews.text: I hate to make statements like this, but here it comes: The Act of Killing may be the strangest documentary you see this year (this decade?).
reviews.author: Clint O'Connor

reviews.text: The cameras bring out the worst in all concerned, who think nothing of singing and dancing about mass murder.
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: This is living history as a surreal pageant.
reviews.author: Peter Galvin

reviews.text: The emotionally manipulative use of some of the material raises all kinds of questions about veracity.
reviews.author: Tony Rayns

reviews.text: One thing's for sure. You won't see another documentary like this one.
reviews.author: Edward Johnson-Ott

reviews.text: Of all the uncomfortable experiences you might endure in the name of understanding the evils of history, this film is arguably the kind that is most necessary.
reviews.author: Ruth Brown

reviews.text: The Act of Killing works brilliantly on many levels, capturing like no other documentary I have seen, like no other film I can imagine, the fevered insanity of those days.
reviews.author: Evan Williams

reviews.text: The originality of The Act of Killing lies in Oppenheimer's decision to treat artifice as a roundabout path to truth.
reviews.author: Jake Wilson

reviews.text: Bizarre, hypnotic, audacious.
reviews.author: James Adams

reviews.text: The emotional places this troubling movie takes him to are rewardingly primal and potent, forcing both subject and viewer to wrestle with internal demons.
reviews.author: Keith Uhlich

reviews.text: I certainly do not move that the film should be suppressed, only that one should know what it is. It is a bath in a smiling madness.
reviews.author: Stanley Kauffmann

reviews.text: A haunting true story confessional doc about the mass killings of a million people depicted as communists in the Indonesia of 1965 and 1966.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: This film is a prime example of how art can succeed where textbooks and historical works sometimes fail. It is also an example of how Hollywood films can inspire murderers to kill thousands of people with style.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: the company films [the killers] re-enacting their murders in the style of American gangster films and lavish musicals, claiming to film them for a movie.
reviews.author: Mark R. Leeper

reviews.text: Extraordinarily original, psychologically acute and profoundly disturbing...
reviews.author: John Beifuss

reviews.text: A truly haunting documentary masterpiece.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: The film is far too long and repetitive, even though it's often gobsmacking in its frank portrayal of these truly nasty, ugly human beings who boast on television about their killings and are ready to keep on killing. Nay, keen to do so
reviews.author: Andrew L. Urban

reviews.text: Probably the most horrifying and, at the same time, compelling movie you're likely to see this year. It's difficult to endure, yet impossible not to watch.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: Director Joshua Oppenheimer shines a light on one of the 20th century's most under-reported atrocities, but his film, years in the making, is so much more than a straightforward history lesson.
reviews.author: Marc Mohan

reviews.text: On the one hand, Congo and his pals are pure, unadulterated evil. Yet they all worked in a system which still embraces them to this day, to an ends where everyone agrees the means were justified.
reviews.author: Bill Gibron

reviews.text: This is a horrifying, unflinching film with Congo serving as the darkest heart of a past that continues to go unpunished and seems ready to repeat itself at any moment.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Oppenheimer captures dozens of shocking, candid moments... My initial reaction was disbelief.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: By turning murder into performance, "The Act of Killing" dramatizes the perverted hearts of these men, the twisted mental leaps they needed to feel okay, and even proud, of what they've done.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: A powerful look at an Indonesian atrocity
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: ..intentionally keeps comprehension at bay, and therein lies its moral forcefulness.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: This stunning "documentary of the imagination" shows Anwar and other thugs staging scenes of torture and murder for the camera.
reviews.author: Bill Stamets

reviews.text: An odd but riveting film that slowly peels back the veneer of one man's tough-guy image and illustrates the very real psychic toll of murder.
reviews.author: Mike Scott

reviews.text: Absolutely shattering.
reviews.author: Anders Wright

reviews.text: In The Act of Killing, director Joshua Oppenheimer pulls off the impossible: He confronts great, incomprehensible evil and puts a human face on it.
reviews.author: Rene Rodriguez

reviews.text: The film absolutely doesn't glamorize this behavior, and it's staggering the matter-of-fact manner with which some of these killers and corruption advocates speak.
reviews.author: Matt Pais

reviews.text: These bizarre images distract from the question at the center of the film: whether it was film-watching itself that carried the seed of all this cruelty.
reviews.author: Richard von Busack

reviews.text: This film is jaw-dropping. It's a must-see.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: The Absurd-Banal-Hideous-O-Meter hits eleven and breaks.
reviews.author: Kelly Vance

reviews.text: The best documentary to grace U.S. screens in years. It's horrifying, riveting, and even, at times, darkly funny.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: The Act of Killing allows the victors a forum to elaborate on their story, and, by their own hands, these aged conquerors unwittingly rewrite aspects of the history that has propped them up for so many decades.
reviews.author: Marjorie Baumgarten

reviews.text: ... a fascinating exploration into the ways that guilt can manifest itself ... a mind-boggling two hours.
reviews.author: Eric Melin

reviews.text: "The Act of Killing" is difficult to watch because it toys with your emotions. These men repel you, yet simultaneously, draw you to them, as they nonchalantly and proudly brag about their work.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: A shocking exhibition of what Hannah Arendt called the banality of evil--or, in this case, the absurdity of evil.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: 'The Act of Killing' is unsettling in drawing in the viewer, in almost humanizing its unrepentant vile inhuman men who in theory did not act for personal motives.
reviews.author: Donald J. Levit

reviews.text: Joshua Oppenheimer's documentary interviews leaders of Indonesian death squads responsible for deaths of millions & has them re-enact the killings. The combination of drama therapy and accidental self-exposure - utterly bizarre, unexpected and valuable.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: [A] unique and unforgettable documentary.
reviews.author: J. R. Jones

reviews.text: The Act of Killing will mesmerize, confound and haunt you. From the opening scenes you'll wonder if what you're watching is real. And by the end you'll wish that it had all been a horrible fever dream.
reviews.author: Matthew Odam

reviews.text: The acts it describes are shocking, the world it shows is shocking and the filmmaking itself is shocking. This is not a film easily forgotten.
reviews.author: Tom Long

reviews.text: There is no sense of remorse in these men for what they did to so many innocent people and that...is chilling.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: Watching these crazy loons make a movie about their crimes against humanity may not be the most pleasant way to spend an evening. But you can't deny that it's utterly fascinating.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: Directors Joshua Oppenheimer and Christine Cynn have created something extraordinary in The Act of Killing, the much-talked-about documentary about torture and murder during the Indonesian dictatorship of the '60s and '70s.
reviews.author: Cary Darling

reviews.text: A horrifying yet mesmerizing work, "The Act of Killing" instructively meanders at times as in a Werner Herzog film.
reviews.author: Tom Keogh

reviews.text: This riveting documentary about political mass murder in Indonesia incorporates the killers' own movie fantasies about their massacres and deepens our understanding of the fascist brain.
reviews.author: Michael Sragow

reviews.text: It is utterly chilling.
reviews.author: Steven Rea

reviews.text: Better characters could hardly have been invented.
reviews.author: Laura Bennett

reviews.text: "The Act of Killing" works on so many levels -- psychodrama, horror movie, Orwellian nightmare, Poe story -- that sifting through your reactions could take days.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: I can't be more direct. "The Act of Killing" is one of the most extraordinary films you'll ever encounter, not to mention one of the craziest filmmaking concepts anywhere, and that includes the whole Bollywood thing.
reviews.author: Janice Page

reviews.text: It's a tough watch, but it's not like anything you've ever seen.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: It's a film that is absolutely hard to watch. It's also a film that absolutely should be seen.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: Anwar Congo may be the scariest person you'll see on screen this year.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: Oppenheimer allows murderous thugs free rein to preen their atrocities, and then fobs it all off as some kind of exalted art thing. This is more than an aesthetic crime; it's a moral crime.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: If director Joshua Oppenheimer occasionally loses his way in his own narrative, where this picture demands attention is in its chilling portrait of indoctrination and evil.
reviews.author: Dustin Putman

reviews.text: Whatever you call it, The Act of Killing is a must-see.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: It's a mind-bending film, devastating and disorienting, that disturbs us in ways we're not used to being disturbed ...
reviews.author: Kenneth Turan

reviews.text: [It] may be one of the most horrifying films you'll ever see, and one of the most edifying.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: It's a gut-wrenching and emotionally exhausting look at impunity that resonates far beyond its obscure central conflict.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: A cynically exploitative film made in the name of human rights, which it has about as much to do with as the Punked show on MTV.
reviews.author: Louis Proyect

reviews.text: Presenting a terrifying view of a hidden holocaust and a moral apocalypse in which the most basic humanities have become twisted beyond recognition, The Act of Killing is a towering achievement in filmmaking, documentary or otherwise.
reviews.author: Jessica Kiang

reviews.text: The magnitude of this achievement, this depiction of a diseased and corrupt society that is in so many ways similar to our own, cannot be understated.
reviews.author: Robert Levin

reviews.text: I have watched hundreds of hours of war crimes, genocides and miscarriages of justice carried out by unremarkable men with dimly lit souls. "The Act of Killing" bids to outdo them all.
reviews.author: Steven Boone

reviews.text: It will leave you breathless.
reviews.author: Linda Barnard

reviews.text: It's a virtually unprecedented social document.
reviews.author: Bob Mondello

reviews.text: The cumulative impact is devastating, and very far from a simple Western condemnation of another country's brutality.
reviews.author: Farran Smith Nehme

reviews.text: Atrocity hides beneath a grandfather's gentle smile in "The Act of Killing," Joshua Oppenheimer's remarkable, unnerving documentary portrait of barbarity and its lasting legacies.
reviews.author: Greg Evans

reviews.text: Among the most profound, formally complex, and emotionally overpowering documentaries I've ever seen.
reviews.author: Dana Stevens

reviews.text: As filming continues, the quiet brilliance behind the assignment comes to light.
reviews.author: Manori Ravindran

reviews.text: Ultimately, The Act Of Killing acknowledges that while Oppenheimer may have subtly tortured their conscience, these thugs are paying no real price.
reviews.author: Noel Murray

reviews.text: Prepare to be shocked, disgusted, enraged and emotionally devastated. It's the most terrifying film in years.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: This chilling documentary, executive produced by Werner Herzog and Errol Morris, has a twisted but illuminating point of entry.
reviews.author: Joe Neumaier

reviews.text: This is not a movie that lets go of you easily.
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: There are good reasons to see The Act of Killing, a new documentary directed by Joshua Oppenheimer, but pleasure is not among them.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: You've never seen anything like The Act of Killing.
reviews.author: Jay Stone

reviews.text: By tackling one man's sense of right and wrong (or lack thereof), Oppenheimer is ultimately tackling human nature.
reviews.author: Ignatiy Vishnevetsky

reviews.text: The film is so shocking and depressing that its subjects' utter disconnection from morality would almost be funny if it wasn't so frightening.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: Remarkably complex documentary about Indonesian genocide has the unrepentant, unpunished perpetrators make a movie about what they did in 1965.
reviews.author: Sarah Sluis

reviews.text: However, by humanizing psychopathic behavior, "The Act of Killing" is unparalleled in its unsettling perspective on the delusions associated with dictatorial extremes.
reviews.author: Eric Kohn

reviews.text: A supreme testament to the cinema's capacity for inquiry, confrontation, and remembrance.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: A surreal, chilling and unprecedented examination of atrocity and accountability, it's difficult to think of another documentary -- or piece of media -- that so thoroughly captures a mass murderer's conscience -- as well as charting its evolution.
reviews.author: Anthony Kaufman

reviews.text: Crime but no punishment in remarkably revealing film about Indonesian death squads.
reviews.author: Stephen Dalton

reviews.text: A blood-boiling look at a crime whose perpetrators remain national heroes in their native Indonesia.
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: "The Act of Killing" is disquieting, uncomfortable ... and riveting."
reviews.author: James Rocchi

reviews.text: The most gut-wrenching 'making of' documentary of all time.
reviews.author: Matt Patches

reviews.text: Bizarre to the point of trippiness, yet it's one of the most lucid portraits of evil I've ever seen.
reviews.author: David Edelstein

reviews.text: At once the most micro and meta combination of cinéma vérité, documentary, and docudrama filmmaking techniques ever assembled, Joshua Oppenheimer's "The Act of Killing" is an earth-shattering cinema experience.
reviews.author: Cole Smithey

reviews.text: As insights into the darkest corners of human mentality go, this is a truly remarkable, real-life alternative to movies like Downfall (the last days of Hitler) and The Last King of Scotland (the Idi Amin story).
reviews.author: Graham Young

reviews.text: Joshua Oppenheimer's The Act of Killing is, at the very least, unlike anything we've seen before. Gruelling, harrowing, and weirdly funny.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: A film that would be a satire were it not so chillingly real.
reviews.author: Ron Wilkinson

reviews.text: The Act of Killing and its backstory no doubt have more to reveal upon closer investigation, though what it's shown is already hard to forget.
reviews.author: Nicolas Rapold

reviews.text: This is an unflinching, captivating documentary that does much more than simply record or readdress history - it uses cinema as both judge and jury for a one-time executioner.
reviews.author: Michael Leader

reviews.text: Opppenheimer's high-risk strategy of avoiding historical analysis and giving the film over to bragging mass murderers pays huge dividends.
reviews.author: Tom Dawson

reviews.text: Unspeakable horror and utterly mundane madness are thrown together in the existential equivalent of the Large Hadron Collider - fact and fiction meeting head on with quietly earth-shattering results.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: Unforgettable. A no-fooling work of genius.
reviews.author: Tara Brady

reviews.text: The director has hit upon a form that renders these atrocities... as unsparing X-rays of the murderers' vast delusions.
reviews.author: Ryan Gilbey

reviews.text: It's one of the most gruelling and disturbing films you will ever see but, if you want the truth, essential.
reviews.author: David Sexton

reviews.text: This ideological push and pull at the film's core supplies it with a sense of high drama. How far can Oppenheimer indulge the whims of his subject to further calcify his demonic inner-nature?
reviews.author: David Jenkins

reviews.text: An astonishing documentary that's essential viewing for anyone wishing to understand the darker aspects of the human condition.
reviews.author: Christopher Tookey

reviews.text: It is a gut-churning film: and a radical dive into history, grabbing the past in a way a conventional documentary would not.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: First, the film beggars belief. Then it sends belief running into the hills, screaming for help and understanding.
reviews.author: Nigel Andrews

reviews.text: This movie is essential.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: Joshua Oppenheimer's film leaves too many questions unanswered but it's a chilling demonstration of the banality of evil and an eye-opening portrait of a corrupt nation.
reviews.author: Henry Fitzherbert

reviews.text: Hopefully there will be as much of a lasting effect on the killers as this picture has on the viewer, in a feature that isn't likely to escape you easily.
reviews.author: Stefan Pape

reviews.text: A sizzling doc that focuses on the repulsive bragging of two unpunished mass murderers treated by their government as heroes.
reviews.author: Harvey S. Karten

reviews.text: You may need a stiff drink and a lie down afterwards.
reviews.author: Mark Stafford

reviews.text: This extraordinary work serves up a series of shocking and surreal sequences, and uses the artifice of filmmaking to expose horrendous truths.
reviews.author: Philip Concannon

reviews.text: Documentary cinema has a new apex.
reviews.author: Blake Howard

reviews.text: The importance of this doco cannot be overstated in exposing a corrupt regime, highlighting the dangers of propaganda and holding a warped mirror to the monsters that walk the Earth as free men
reviews.author: Cameron Williams

reviews.text: The brutal honesty that fills The Act Of Killing is a true testament to Joshua Oppenheimer's crafty documentarian skills which emotionally break characters down without them even knowing.
reviews.author: Matt Donato

reviews.text: A startling wake-up call to the pornography of violence and its major role in crimes against humanity.
reviews.author: Frederic and Mary Ann Brussat

reviews.text: In Joshua Oppenheimer's extraordinary The Act of Killing, film becomes the medium for a bold historical reckoning--and in more ways than one.
reviews.author: Andrew Schenker

reviews.text: The Act of Killing is about the horrific past that warped and still rules Indonesia's present, but it's also about the stories we all construct so we can live with ourselves.
reviews.author: Elise Nakhnikian

reviews.text: One of this decade's most important and most harrowing documentaries, The Act of Killing is a shattering take on the nature of evil.
reviews.author: Jason Gorber

reviews.text: Almost every frame is astonishing.
reviews.author: Catherine Shoard

reviews.text: A minor miracle
reviews.author: Jordan Hoffman

synopsis: Filmmakers expose the horrifying mass executions of accused communists in Indonesia and those who are celebrated in their country for perpetrating the crime.
